# Tier `rockchip-rk3588`

## Serving

| setting | value | what it controls |
|---|---|---|
| backend | `rk3588` | which `llama-swap.*.yaml` template renders |
| ctx_size | 8192 | the served window (`--ctx-size`) |
| kv_type | `f16` | `--cache-type-k/v`, kept symmetric |
| flash_attn | `off` | `--flash-attn` (required for a q8_0 V cache) |
| resident_tier | `qwen3.5-2b-npu` | the model that stays hot; seeds the agent planner seat (agent_model) when it differs from the workhorse |
| agent_ctx_tokens | 8192 | the agent's `-ctx-tokens` compaction budget |
| 26B-A4B | dropped | whether the 26B MoE is served, and where its experts live |

## Agent seat

This tier declares no persistent vLLM agent seat: the agent lane runs on the
llama.cpp seat named by `agent_model` above, in the tier's own llama-swap config.

## Media

This tier serves these media **seats** — models in its own llama-swap config, rendered
at install time. Each seat also produces the harness config binding that routes to it, so a
binding can never name a seat that was not rendered:

| seat | kind | binds | model | residency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `qwen3.5-2b-npu` | rkllm | `vision_model` | `qwen3.5-2b_w8a8_rk3588.rkllm` | swappable |

An `rkllm` seat runs on the NPU through the Rockchip RKLLM runtime, not in llama.cpp. It is
started with its own window and a `cpu_mask` — the CPUs the runtime's host threads may use
(at least 3, the runtime refuses fewer than the SoC has NPU cores):

- `qwen3.5-2b-npu`: window 16384, `cpu_mask` `0x0f`, vision encoder `qwen3.5-2b_vision_rk3588.rknn`

A seat still needs its weights on the box — model downloads stay out-of-band, as with
every seed.

The installer seeds this tier's media bindings (`config_seed`):

| key | value |
|---|---|
| `musicgen_script` | `` |
| `run_graph_script` | `` |
| `sdcpp_script` | `` |
| `upscale_script` | `` |
| `videogen_script` | `` |
| `voicegen_script` | `` |

`__OFFLOAD_HOME__` is replaced with the install root at render time.

## Installer-seeded config (non-media)

These `config_seed` keys are applied to a FRESH harness config exactly like the media

## Operator notes

Recorded with the profile — several are measurements from real hardware,
including reasons a tempting change was deliberately not made.

> Rockchip RK3588 SoC board (reference: an Orange Pi 5, RK3588S): 4x Cortex-A55 (cpu0-3) + 4x Cortex-A76 (cpu4-7), 7.7 GiB LPDDR4X shared by CPU, GPU and NPU (no dedicated VRAM), a 3-core 6 TOPS NPU and a Mali-G610 MP4 GPU. The board also runs the operator's home-automation stack, which decides the shape of the tier: NO model runs on the CPU (ADR 0054 amendment: no alt_backends, no CPU seat), uma_reserve_gib 3 holds RAM back for that stack (fleet-serve advertises MemTotal less the reserve as capacity and MemAvailable less it as free, about 4.7 GiB of inference budget), and every model unloads after five idle minutes (ttl 300). Detection reads the device tree's root compatible: `rockchip,rk3588` on the vendor 6.1 kernel (board token rockchip,rk3588s-orangepi-5), `rockchip,rk3588s` on mainline 7.0 (board token xunlong,orangepi-5); both boot entries classify. NPU (the serving accelerator today): chat and vision run on the Rockchip RKLLM runtime through accelerators/rknpu/rkllm_server.py (rkllm seat qwen3.5-2b-npu, Qwen3.5-2B W8A8, a chat model and a VLM), and image classification, detection and embedding run on the rknpu accelerator sidecar (accelerators/rknpu/server.py). The NPU driver is built into the vendor kernel and is the out-of-tree rknpu 0.9.8 DKMS module on mainline; the in-tree rocket driver is a different stack that neither runtime uses. Qwen3.5-2B W8A8 is the largest RKLLM model that fits the budget (Qwen3.5-4B W8A8 is 5.58 GB, Gemma-4-E2B W8A8 7.98 GB; RK3588 has no W4 path). MEASURED 2026-09-30, mainline 7.0 + rknpu 0.9.8, RKLLM 1.3.1, one 1,256-token prompt: Qwen3.5-2B cpu_mask 0x0f (A55 x4) prefill 22.7 / decode 7.71 tok/s, 0xf0 (A76 x4) 126.4 / 7.14, VmHWM 2,260 MB at a 4096 window; Qwen3.5-0.8B 0x0f 44.5 / 9.07, 0xf0 174.5 / 16.67 (VmHWM 1,178 MB), and on the vendor 6.1 kernel with rknpu 0.9.7 the 0.8B read 0x0f 40.9 / 12.2, 0xe0 (A76 x3) 166.9 / 11.3, 0xf0 200.1 / 18.7, so mainline costs 10-15 % on this path. RKLLM refuses fewer enabled CPUs than the 3 NPU cores, so a cpu_mask needs at least three bits; the tier default is the A55 cluster 0x0f (strict CPU reservation for the host's own stack), which costs the 2B about 5x on prefill against the A76 cluster; the operator decides that trade. GPU, MEASURED 2026-09-30 and BLOCKED: the vendor kernel exposes the Mali as mali_kbase with an OpenCL blob only; mainline 7.0 uses panthor with Mesa 25.2.8 panvk (Vulkan 1.4, conformance 1.4.1.2, 'Mali-G610' as device 0, llvmpipe as device 1). llama.cpp b11270 built with GGML_VULKAN loads there, but its FIRST compute submission never finishes: panthor logs 'job timeout' and llama.cpp aborts with vk::DeviceLostError, on Qwen3.5-2B, Qwen3.5-4B and Gemma-4-E2B Q4 GGUFs alike, with flash-attn on or off and with batches down to 32 tokens on a freshly reset GPU. So this tier renders NO llama.cpp entry; its own template (llama-swap.linux-rk3588.yaml, not the stock vulkan one, which always renders offload-e4b at ~5 GB plus KV) keeps the Vulkan conventions for the day a Mesa/panthor/llama.cpp combination passes on this silicon. Re-measure before adding a GPU entry. vLLM has no Mali or RKNPU target, so this tier declares no vllm_seat. The media scripts this box cannot run (no ComfyUI, no sd.cpp, no TTS engine, no CPU inference) are seeded blank so the node does not advertise their lanes. NOT MEASURED: the 2B's resident size at its full 16384 window, its answer quality against another tier's seat, the vision path's answers, and any agent seat (fleet_agent_enabled is false; none has been chosen).
